SHORT_DESCRIPTION: VN GREEN HOLDINGS PTE. LTD.
PROJECT_TITLE: VN GREEN HOLDINGS PTE. LTD.
LONG_DESCRIPTION:
VN Green Holdings Pte. Ltd. (VNGH or the Company), is a Vietnam-focused, Singapore-based dedicated renewable energy (RE) platform founded in 2020 and wholly owned by Dragon Capital Group Limited (DCG). VNGH currently owns 49.5 MWp Quang Tri solar power plant located in Quang Tri province.  VNGHs strategy is to own at least 300 MW of RE capacity in Vietnam by 2024 through the acquisition of operating wind and solar power projects and by developing greenfield RE projects.      International Finance Corporation (IFC) - the private sector arm of the World Bank Group - is considering a senior, secured corporate loan to VNGH to finance the acquisition of (i) 40 MWp Mui Ne solar project, (ii) 33.1 MWp VSP II solar project, and (iii) other RE projects in Vietnam (the Project).:The Project has an anticipated AIMM rating of Satisfactory.
The main expected project-level outcome stems from preserving and maximizing
positive environmental effects by optimizing the performance of operating solar
projects. Beyond the Project, by structuring the A loan as a certified green
loan according to the internationally recognized green loan principles
(GLP),  the proposed investment is expected to increase integration by
promoting green financing in a market with large climate-smart investment needs
but limited local green financing capacity.

The training content is geared towards the needs of the participants to further develop their project ideas and includes a critical analysis and discussion of the overall socio-political framework. LONG_DESCRIPTION: The objective is to improve the capacity of electricity supply to meet the increasing load demand in the future, reduce power loss, ensure quality and reliability of electricity supply and reduce the selling price to households. The project has been on the drawing board for some time. The original total loan amount was estimated to be about EUR 6.0 million (1999). The project was divided into two phases and the first phase (EUR 3.5 million) has supposedly already been implemented. ELTEL applied in January 2004 for a buyer credit guarantee for the remaining amount of EUR 2.5 million but later (2005) the size of the project was raised to about EUR 9.4 million and the concessional credit requirement to about EUR 7.2 million. The present Feasibility Study proposes a concessional credit of about EUR 6.5 million.
